metadata.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
metadata.purpose: To establish Rent Authority to regulate renting of premises and to protect the interests of landlords and tenants and to provide speedy adjudication mechanism for resolution of disputes.

definitions.landlord: A person who receives or is entitled to receive rent of any premises on his own account. Includes successor-in-interest, trustee, guardian, or receiver.
definitions.tenant: A person by whom or on whose account rent is payable. Includes sub-tenant and person continuing in possession after termination (unless eviction order made). Excludes persons against whom eviction decree exists.
definitions.premises: Any building or part thereof let on rent for residential or commercial use. Includes garden, garage, parking, vacant land, fittings. EXCLUDES hotel, lodging house, dharamshala, inn, industrial use.
definitions.rent_authority: Officer appointed under Section 30 (Deputy Collector rank).
definitions.rent_court: Constituted under Section 33 (Additional District Magistrate rank).
definitions.property_manager: Person/entity authorized by landlord to manage premises and represent landlord.
definitions.security_deposit: Amount paid in advance by tenant, refundable upon vacating.

list: Premises owned by Central/State Govt, UT Admin, Local Authority, Govt Undertaking, Statutory Body, Cantonment Board
Premises owned by Company/University/Org given to employees as part of service contract
Premises owned by Religious/Charitable institutions (specified by notification)
Premises owned by Auqaf (Waqf Act 1995) or Public Trusts
Other buildings exempted in public interest by notification
exemptions.opt_in_clause: Owner and tenant of exempted premises MAY agree to be regulated under this Act by informing Rent Authority.

sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.content: Extends to whole State/UT. Commences on date appointed by State Govt/UT Admin.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.content: Defines Landlord, Tenant, Premises, Rent Authority, Rent Court, Rent Tribunal, Property Manager, etc.

sections.title: Act not to apply to certain premises
sections.content: Lists exemptions (Govt, Service Quarters, Religious, Waqf, etc.). Opt-in allowed.

sections.title: Tenancy agreement
sections.content: MANDATORY written agreement for all tenancies after commencement. Must be informed to Rent Authority jointly by landlord/tenant within 2 months (or separately within 1 month if joint fails). Rent Authority provides Unique ID and uploads details within 7 working days. Information is conclusive proof of tenancy facts.
sections.pramaan_flag: If lease lacks written agreement or Unique ID, flag as 'Non-compliant with Section 4'.

sections.title: Period of tenancy
sections.content: Valid for period agreed in agreement. Tenant may request renewal. If fixed term ends and tenant fails to vacate, liable for enhanced rent (Section 23). Force majeure extension: Landlord must allow tenant to stay 1 month after disaster ceases on same terms.

sections.title: Rights and obligations of successor in case of death
sections.content: Agreement binding on successors of deceased landlord/tenant for remaining period.

sections.title: Restriction on subletting
sections.content: Tenant CANNOT sublet or transfer rights without supplementary agreement with landlord. Sub-tenancy must be informed to Rent Authority within 2 months.
sections.pramaan_flag: Flag 'Subletting without consent' clauses as illegal.

sections.title: Rent payable
sections.content: Rent as agreed in tenancy agreement.

sections.title: Revision of rent
sections.content: As per agreement. If landlord incurs expenditure for improvement/addition (agreed in writing prior), rent may increase effective 1 month after work completion.

sections.title: Rent Authority to determine revised rent in case of dispute
sections.content: Rent Authority determines revised rent/charges on application.

sections.title: Security deposit
content: Residential: NOT exceed 2 months rent.
Non-residential: NOT exceed 6 months rent.
Refund: On date of taking over vacant possession, after deducting tenant liabilities.
sections.pramaan_flag: CRITICAL: Flag any clause demanding >2 months (residential) or >6 months (commercial) deposit as ILLEGAL under Section 11(1). Flag 'Non-refundable deposit' as ILLEGAL under Section 11(2).

chapters.title: RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF LANDLORD AND TENANT

sections.title: Original tenancy agreement to be retained
sections.content: Signed in duplicate; one each retained by landlord and tenant.

sections.title: Rent payment and receipt
sections.content: Tenant pays within agreed period. Landlord/Manager MUST provide signed receipt immediately. Electronic bank acknowledgment is conclusive proof.

sections.title: Deposit of rent with Rent Authority
sections.content: If landlord refuses rent/receipt, tenant pays via money order for 2 months; if still refused, deposits with Rent Authority. Rent Authority enquires and passes orders.

sections.title: Repair and maintenance
content: Landlord/Tenant keep premises in good condition (except normal wear/tear).
Responsibilities as per Second Schedule or agreement.
If tenant fails repairs, landlord deducts from security deposit (payable within 1 month of notice).
If landlord refuses repairs, tenant carries out and deducts from rent (max 50% of monthly rent).
If uninhabitable without repairs and landlord refuses, tenant may abandon after 15 days notice.
Force majeure: Landlord cannot charge rent until premises restored to habitable.
sections.pramaan_flag: Flag clauses shifting ALL structural repairs to tenant as potentially void against Section 15(1) and Second Schedule Part A.

sections.title: Tenant to look after premises
sections.content: Tenant must not damage premises, inform landlord of damage, take reasonable care.

sections.title: Entry into premises
content: Landlord/Manager may enter after 24 hours written/electronic notice for: repairs, inspection, other reasonable cause.
Notice must specify day, time, reason.
NO entry before sunrise or after sunset.
Exception: Emergent situations (war, flood, fire, etc.) allow entry without notice.
sections.pramaan_flag: CRITICAL: Flag 'Landlord may enter at any time without notice' as ILLEGAL under Section 17(1). Flag 'Entry after sunset' as ILLEGAL under Section 17(2).

sections.title: Information as to property manager
sections.content: Landlord must provide tenant: Manager name, proof of authorization, specific purposes, period, entity details (if legal entity).

sections.title: Duties of property manager
sections.content: Collect rent (with receipt), essential repairs, inspect, give notices (maintenance, delay, revision, vacation, renewal), help resolve disputes. Acts only on landlord instructions. Rent Authority can remove manager for violation.

sections.title: Withholding essential supply or service
content: Landlord/Manager CANNOT withhold essential supply/service.
Essential services: Water, electricity, piped gas, lights (passages/lifts/staircase), conservancy, parking, communication links, sanitary services, security fixtures.
Remedy: Tenant applies to Rent Authority → Interim order for immediate restoration → Enquiry within 1 month → Compensation up to 2 months rent.
Penalty for frivolous application by tenant: Up to 2x monthly rent.
sections.pramaan_flag: CRITICAL: Flag 'Landlord may disconnect utilities for rent default' as ILLEGAL under Section 20(1).

sections.title: Eviction grounds
content: Tenant not evicted during tenancy unless agreed or under Section 21(2)/22.
Grounds for Rent Court eviction order:
(a) Tenant refuses to pay agreed rent
(b) Arrears of rent/charges for 2 consecutive months + interest not paid within 1 month of demand notice
(c) Parted with possession without written consent
(d) Continued misuse after notice (encroachment, nuisance, damage, immoral/illegal use)
(e) Necessary repair/construction/rebuilding requires vacation (reoccupation only if new agreement submitted)
(f) Required for repair/change of use due to land use change by competent authority
(g) Tenant gave notice to vacate and landlord contracted to sell/took steps suffering serious interest loss
(h) Structural change/permanent structure erected without written consent
Relief: No eviction for arrears if tenant pays/deposits within 1 month of notice. Relief lost if tenant fails again within same year.
Partial eviction allowed for ground (e) if landlord agrees.
sections.pramaan_flag: Flag 'Eviction without court order' or 'Eviction for reasons not listed in Section 21(2)' as illegal procedure.

sections.title: Eviction in case of death of landlord
sections.content: Legal heirs may apply for eviction if bonafide requirement during tenancy period. Rent Court passes order if satisfied.

sections.title: Enhancement of rent in case of refusal to vacate
sections.content: If tenant fails to vacate on expiry/termination: (a) 2x monthly rent for first 2 months; (b) 4x monthly rent thereafter.
sections.pramaan_flag: Verify penalty clauses match Section 23 rates.

sections.title: Refund of advance rent
sections.content: Landlord must refund advance rent/payment before recovery of possession (deducting dues). Failure → Simple interest at prescribed rate.

sections.title: Payment of rent during eviction proceedings
sections.content: For grounds other than (a)/(b), if tenant contests, landlord may apply for order directing tenant to pay rent/charges/penalties during proceedings.

sections.title: Permission to build additional structures
sections.content: Tenant cannot erect permanent structure without consent. If landlord proposes improvement and tenant refuses, landlord applies to Rent Court. Court permits if ready/willing and no undue hardship/deterioration to tenant. Tenant responsible for removing unauthorized structures.

sections.title: Special provision regarding vacant land
sections.content: If premises includes vacant land permissible for building, and landlord unable to get possession, may apply to Rent Court. Court may sever land, place landlord in possession, determine rent for rest, if no undue hardship.

sections.title: Vacant possession to landlord
sections.content: Order for recovery binding on all occupants. Vacant possession must be given by all.

sections.title: Notice of giving up possession by tenant
sections.content: Tenant gives written notice as per agreement. If no stipulation, at least 1 month notice.

sections.title: Rent Authority
sections.content: District Collector/Magistrate appoints officer (not below Deputy Collector rank) as Rent Authority.

sections.title: Power and procedure
sections.content: Rent Authority has powers of Rent Court for proceedings under Sections 4, 9, 10, 14, 15, 19, 20. Procedure per Sections 35, 36.

sections.title: Appeals
sections.content: Appeal against Rent Authority order to Rent Court within 30 days.

sections.title: Rent Court
sections.content: District Collector/Magistrate appoints Additional Collector/ADM (equivalent rank) as Rent Court.

sections.title: Rent Tribunal
sections.content: State Govt/UT Admin appoints District Judge/Additional District Judge as Rent Tribunal.

sections.title: Procedure
content: CPC 1908 does not apply (except service of summons). Guided by natural justice.
Application/Appeal with affidavit/docs → Notice to opposite party → Reply → Rejoinder → Hearing/Summary inquiry.
Disposal target: 60 days from receipt (reasons recorded if exceeded).
Evidence by affidavit (witness examination only if necessary for justice).
Max 3 adjournments per party (costs imposed if reasonable cause).
Specific timelines: Eviction applications (21(2)(a,b,e,f,g) & 22) decided within 90 days. Applications (21(2)(c,d)) decided within 30 days.

sections.title: Powers
content: Same powers as Civil Court (CPC 1908): Summoning, discovery, commissions, affidavits, dismissal/ex-parte, execution, review, revision.
Deemed judicial proceeding (IPC 193, 228, 196). Deemed Civil Court for CrPC 195, Ch XXVI.
Inspection: 24h notice, enter premises sunrise-sunset.
Assessors/Valuers may be appointed.
Clerical errors correctable.
Fine recovery powers of Judicial Magistrate 1st Class.
Orders executable as civil court decree.
Ex-parte orders set aside if notice not served/sufficient cause.
Orders final subject to appeal (no original suit questioning).

sections.title: Appeal to Rent Tribunal
sections.content: Appeal against Rent Court order to Rent Tribunal within 30 days. Notice served, hearing within 30 days, disposed within 60 days. Documents allowed once if necessary. Interlocutory orders possible. Confirm/set aside/modify.

sections.title: Execution of order
content: Rent Court executes orders (delivery of possession, attach bank accounts, appoint advocate/officer).
Local Govt/Police help allowed (applicant pays costs).
Summary manner, disposed within 30 days of notice service.

sections.title: Officers and employees
sections.content: State Govt/UT Admin determines/appoints officers for Rent Authority/Court/Tribunal.

sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred
sections.content: No civil court suit/proceeding regarding provisions of this Act. Rent Court jurisdiction limited to tenancy agreements submitted (First Schedule); no title/ownership questions.

sections.title: Court fees
sections.content: Court Fees Act 1870 applies. Recovery application/Appeal memo deemed suit between landlord/tenant. Rent Authority application fee = interlocutory application in civil court.

sections.title: Public servants
sections.content: Members of Rent Authority/Court/Tribunal deemed public servants (IPC Section 21).

sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
sections.content: No suit/prosecution against person/Authority/Court/Tribunal for good faith actions under Act.

sections.title: Power to make rules
sections.content: State Govt/UT Admin makes rules (previous publication). Matters: Digital platform form, rent payment/deposit methods, eviction application forms, interest rate for refund, vacant land application form, Court/Tribunal application forms, execution manner, etc.

sections.title: Laying of rules
sections.content: Rules laid before State Legislature/UT Legislature.

sections.title: Power to remove difficulties
sections.content: State Govt/UT Admin may remove difficulties by order (Gazette) within 2 years of commencement. Order laid before Legislature.

sections.title: Repeal and savings
sections.content: Existing State/UT Rent Control Act repealed. Pending cases continued/disposed under old Act as if it continued.

first_schedule.title: Form for Information of Tenancy (Section 4)
fields: Other charges (Electricity, Water, Extra furnishing, Other services)
Enclosures: Tenancy Agreement, Self-attested PAN/Aadhaar copies, Photographs

second_schedule.title: Division of Maintenance Responsibility (Section 15)
part_a_landlord_responsibilities: Internal/external electrical wiring and related maintenance when necessary
part_b_tenant_responsibilities: Repairs/replacement of electrical equipment (except major wiring)
Maintenance of gardens/open spaces let to/used by tenant

pramaan_integration_notes.usage: This JSON serves as the 'Official Rule' source for the Pramaan Engine when auditing Rental Lease Agreements.

matching_strategy.deposit_check: Match 'Security Deposit' amount against Section 11 limits (2 months residential / 6 months commercial). Flag excess. Flag 'Non-refundable' clauses as illegal per Section 11(2).
matching_strategy.entry_clause_check: Match 'Landlord Entry' clause against Section 17. Flag 'Any time without notice' or 'After sunset' as illegal.
matching_strategy.utility_cutoff_check: Match 'Utility Disconnection' clause against Section 20. Flag 'Disconnect for rent default' as illegal.
matching_strategy.lock_in_check: Match 'Lock-in Period' clause. While not explicitly banned, ensure it doesn't violate Section 5 (period as agreed) or Section 29 (1 month notice to vacate). Flag absolute lock-ins preventing vacancy as risky.
matching_strategy.maintenance_check: Match 'Repair Responsibility' against Second Schedule. Flag clauses shifting Part A (Structural/Wiring/Pipes) entirely to tenant as void against Section 15(1).
matching_strategy.eviction_check: Match 'Eviction Grounds' against Section 21(2). Flag grounds not listed (e.g., 'Landlord needs for personal use' without bonafide requirement proof under Section 22) as potentially unenforceable.
matching_strategy.agreement_registration: Check if agreement mentions 'Informed to Rent Authority' or has Unique ID per Section 4. Flag absence as non-compliant.
